                    text: [32m"# Create recurring tasks with Encore's Cron Jobs API\n"[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-05-05, [Read more](https://encore.dev/docs/go/primitives/cron-jobs)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'`$ encore app create --example=uptime`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To define a Cron Job, import the `encore.dev/cron` package, and call the `cron.NewJob()` function and store it as a package-level variable.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Example\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import "encore.dev/cron"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Send a welcome email to everyone who signed up in the last two hours.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'var _ = cron.NewJob("welcome-email", cron.JobConfig{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Title: "Send welcome emails",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Every: 2 * cron.Hour,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Endpoint: SendWelcomeEmail,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// SendWelcomeEmail emails everyone who signed up recently.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"// It's idempotent: it only sends a welcome email to each person once.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api private\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func SendWelcomeEmail(ctx context.Context) error {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return nil\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Run the monthly accounting sync job at 4am (UTC) on the 15th day of each month.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'var _ = cron.NewJob("accounting-sync", cron.JobConfig{\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# cron package - encore.dev/cron - Go Packages\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Package cron provides support for cron jobs: recurring tasks that run on a schedule.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### func NewJob ¶\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func NewJob(id string, jobConfig JobConfig) (_ *Job)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'NewJob defines a new cron job.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It is specially recognized by the Encore Parser\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and results in the Encore Platform provisioning the cron job on next deploy.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The id argument is a unique identifier you give to each cron job.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To define a new cron job, call NewJob and assign it a package-level variable:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import "encore.dev/cron"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Send a welcome email to everyone who signed up in the last two hours.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'var _ = cron.NewJob("welcome-email", cron.JobConfig{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Title: "Send welcome emails",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Every: 2 * cron.Hour,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Endpoint: SendWelcomeEmail,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// SendWelcomeEmail emails everyone who signed up recently.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"// It's idempotent: it only sends a welcome email to each person once.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api private\n'[39m +
                      [32m'func SendWelcomeEmail(ctx context.Context) error {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return nil\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m"# Encore Changelog — It's about time — Cron Jobs are here!\n"[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-03-02, last updated: 2025-09-04, [Read more](https://encore.dev/changelog/v0.19.0-its-about-time)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Encore provides native support for these types of use cases using Cron Jobs.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's how easy it is:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import "encore.dev/cron"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Send a welcome email to everyone who signed up in the last two hours.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'var _ = cron.NewJob("welcome-email", cron.JobConfig{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Title: "Send welcome emails",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Every: 2 * cron.Hour,\n'[39m +

                      [32m"That's it!\n"[39m +
                      [32m'When this is deployed, Encore will call the\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Building a fully Type-Safe Event-Driven Backend in Go\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-11-10, last updated: 2026-05-05, [Read more](https://dev.to/encore/building-a-fully-type-safe-event-driven-backend-in-go-2g8m)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"We'll create a new `CheckAll` API endpoint in the `monitor` service that will list all the tracked sites and check all of them.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'🥐 Create the new `CheckAll` endpoint inside `monitor/check.go`:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import "golang.org/x/sync/errgroup"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// CheckAll checks all sites.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'//encore:api public method=POST path=/checkall\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'resp, err := site.List(ctx)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if err != nil {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return err\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// Check up to 8 sites concurrently.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'g, ctx := errgroup.WithContext(ctx)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'g.SetLimit(8)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +

                [32m"I'm refining the understanding of Go cron job endpoint requirements. It's clear now that these functions can only accept `context.Context` and must return either `error` or a value with an `error`. This specificity is quite helpful.\n"[39m +

                [32m'**Implementing Cleanup Logic**\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'I\'m focusing on the practical implementation of the cron job\'s cleanup endpoint. It\'s confirmed that a public API, `POST /cleanup`, will house the deletion logic for records older than 24 hours. I\'m also exploring the best way to define the cron job\'s schedule, considering both `Every: 1 * cron.Hour` and `Schedule: "0 * * * *"`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**Defining API Contracts**\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"I'm solidifying the request and response structures for our `POST /records` endpoint. It seems the intention is to return the newly created record, mirroring the `CreateRecordResponse` I drafted, rather than just a success status. This provides immediate feedback.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**Designing List Response**\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"I'm now focusing on the structure for listing records. The response will be a JSON object containing an array of `Record` structs, each with `id`, `data`, and `created_at`. An empty slice will be used for no records, ensuring `[]` instead of `null` in the JSON.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**Confirming Package Naming**\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"I'm confirming that the package name should indeed be `cleanup`, matching its directory. This detail is crucial for code organization and import paths. I'm also reviewing the `POST /records` endpoint definition for correctness.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**Handling Record Creation**\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"I've refined the `POST /records` endpoint. It's now idempotent, using `ON CONFLICT` to update existing records rather than erroring, which is crucial for robustness when users resubmit IDs. The response will return the complete, updated record.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +

            [32m'## Task States and Management\n'[39m +
